Q: How to backfill missing values from another record in Oracle SQL A:

It looks to me that your p table is related to some other table that containes all product_id(s).
Something like, possibly, table products:

ID SHORT_DESC
AA103 short 103
AA104 short 104
AA105 short 105
AA1101 short 1101
AA1103 short 1103
AA1105 short 1105
AA1107 short 1107
AA1108 short 1108
AA1110 short 1110
AA1112 short 1112
AA1114 short 1114

... now if in your p table some of ids are not present:

PRODUCT_ID LONG_DESC
AA103 long desc 103
AA104 long desc 104
AA1101 long desc 1101
AA1107 long desc 1107
AA1110 long desc 1110
AA1114 long 1114

... you can select from the table containing all ids (products) and left join your related table (p) in which case you could use Max() Over() analytic function with windowing clause to get your last previous long_desc for a set of rows filtered in where clause in any way that suits you.

  • assuming that the data looks like in your sample (regarding order of product_id(s) in particular)
Select prod.id as product_id, 
       Max(p.long_desc) Over(Order By prod.id Rows Between Unbounded Preceding And Current Row) as long_desc
From   products prod
Left Join p p ON p.product_id = prod.id
Where prod.id IN('AA103','AA105','AA1101','AA1107','AA1112')
Order By prod.id

R e s u l t :

PRODUCT_ID LONG_DESC
AA103 long desc 103
AA105 long desc 103
AA1101 long desc 1101
AA1107 long desc 1107
AA1112 long desc 1107

Q: Does lua have something like python's slice A:

Working with Lua when coming from Python some times requires a shift of mindset. Lua has few tools that do many things, Python has many specialized language constructs and standard library functions, but they can both do the same things if you know the tricks for each language.

For example, if you say you want a slice without looping through it, what do you really mean? If you extract a slice from an integer-indexed table you will most likely need to loop over it to do anything with it. So, instead of "extracting" the slice to a separate variable and then operating on it, you can directly iterate over a range of indices and do what you need to do:

b = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5}
for i = 1, 4 do something_with(b[i]) end

Q: populate multidimensional struct array with array data A:

You need to append it like this.

for i in 0..<serverStatusMain.count {
    myServerInfo.append(serverInfo(pings: pings[i], serverStatusMain: serverStatusMain[i], statusImageMain: statusImagesMain[i]))
}

There are 2 things to fix:

  • You need i to have the index of the array to iterate through it.

  • You need to append an instance of an array for which you don't need to enclose it within [].

However if you need to append an array you can do it using the other append method.

myServerInfo.append(contentsOf: serverInfoArray) // serverInfoArrat would be an array -> [serverInfo]
